The terminal module (apps/core-app/src/main/modules/terminal) is stuck without the @xterm/xterm 5.5+ fixes for Chromium canvas/WebGL renderer changes, and every install emits a deprecation warning. Any future Electron/Chromium change to canvas text metrics cannot be fixed by upgrading, only by migrating the package name.
recommendation: Migrate to @xterm/xterm and @xterm/addon-fit (import path and addon class names change).

title: plugins/touch-music also pins deprecated xterm@5.3.0 / xterm-addon-fit@0.8.0
summary: The music plugin carries the same retired xterm packages as core-app, and it does not appear to render a terminal at all.
evidence: plugins/touch-music/package.json:26 `"xterm": "^5.3.0",` :27 `"xterm-addon-fit": "^0.8.0"`, both flagged in pnpm-lock.yaml:13819/13813 as `deprecated: This package is now deprecated. Move to @xterm/xterm instead.`
failure_scenario: The plugin bundles a deprecated, unmaintained terminal emulator (~300KB) into its Surface build. Because the dependency is unused by the plugin's feature set, it is pure deprecated surface area that will keep failing dependency audits and blocks the @xterm migration from being completed repo-wide.
recommendation: Remove xterm/xterm-addon-fit from touch-music if unused, otherwise migrate with core-app.

title: tuff-cli and tuff-cli-core depend on deprecated glob@10.5.0 flagged for known vulnerabilities
summary: Both CLI packages declare glob ^10, which npm marks deprecated with an explicit security notice; glob 11 is the supported line.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:40 `"glob": "^10.5.0",` and packages/tuff-cli/package.json:39 `"glob": "^10.5.0",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:8931 `glob@10.5.0: ... deprecated: Old versions of glob are not supported, and contain widely publicized security vulnerabilities, which have been fixed in the current version. Please update.`
failure_scenario: @talex-touch/tuff-cli is published to npm (v0.0.7, publishConfig access public) and is the documented plugin build tool, so every plugin author installs the deprecated glob transitively. Installs emit the deprecation warning and the package cannot receive upstream fixes without a major bump.
recommendation: Move both packages to glob ^11 (the v10 to v11 API is compatible for the patterns used here) and drop the unused @types/glob ^8.1.0 pin.

title: touch-translation depends on deprecated unplugin-vue-router@0.16.2 (merged into vue-router v5)
summary: The translation plugin's route generation relies on a package upstream has retired by folding it into vue-router itself.
evidence: plugins/touch-translation/package.json:42 `"unplugin-vue-router": "^0.16.2",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:12990 `unplugin-vue-router@0.16.2: ... deprecated: 'Merged into vuejs/router. Migrate: https://router.vuejs.org/guide/migration/v4-to-v5.html'`. The plugin runs vue-router ^4.6.4 (plugins/touch-translation/package.json:23).
failure_scenario: The plugin's build is pinned to an abandoned route generator while the rest of the workspace stays on vue-router 4. When core-app moves to vue-router 5 (apps/core-app/package.json:133 also pins ^4.6.4), the deprecated plugin's generated route types diverge from the router's built-in typed routes and the plugin Surface fails to typecheck (`vue-tsc --noEmit`, plugins/touch-translation/package.json:12).
recommendation: Follow the upstream v4-to-v5 migration and drop unplugin-vue-router, or pin the plugin's build to the last compatible combination and document it.

title: touch-translation uses unplugin-vue-macros ^2.x whose @vue-macros core is deprecated
summary: The 2.x macro toolchain resolves to @vue-macros packages that upstream marks deprecated in favour of v3.
evidence: plugins/touch-translation/package.json:41 `"unplugin-vue-macros": "^2.14.5",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:6153-6155 `'@vue-macros/define-props@4.0.6': ... deprecated: Use v3` with `peerDependencies: '@vue-macros/reactivity-transform': ^1.1.6`.
failure_scenario: The macro transforms run inside the plugin's Vite 7 build against Vue 3.5. The deprecated 2.x line will not receive fixes for Vue 3.6+ compiler-sfc changes, so the plugin's Surface build breaks on the next Vue minor while every other workspace package (which uses no macros) keeps building.
recommendation: Upgrade to unplugin-vue-macros v3, or remove the macro plugin if the plugin does not actually use the macros.

title: @ungap/structured-clone@1.3.0 (deprecated, CWE-502) is installed but not pinned by overrides
summary: The root pnpm.overrides block pins ~70 transitive packages for exactly this class of problem, yet a transitive dependency carrying an explicit deprecation-with-CVE notice is not among them.
evidence: pnpm-lock.yaml:5785-5787 `'@ungap/structured-clone@1.3.0': resolution: ... deprecated: Potential CWE-502 - Update to 1.3.1 or higher`. The root override list (package.json:133-195) pins node-forge, form-data, cookie, tar, ws, qs, follow-redirects and many others, but contains no `@ungap/structured-clone` entry.
failure_scenario: @ungap/structured-clone is pulled in through the remark/rehype chain used by apps/nexus content rendering and the root markdown tooling. Its 1.3.0 deserialization path is the flagged CWE-502 vector, and because there is no override, every fresh install keeps resolving 1.3.0 rather than the fixed 1.3.1.
recommendation: Add `"@ungap/structured-clone": "1.3.1"` to pnpm.overrides alongside the existing transitive pins.

title: Three publicly published packages declare no engines field despite a Node >=24.15 workspace
summary: @talex-touch/utils, @talex-touch/tuffex and @talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin are all published to npm without an engines field, so npm/pnpm cannot warn consumers who are on an unsupported Node.
evidence: packages/utils/package.json (v1.0.50, `"private": false`) has no `engines` key; packages/tuffex/package.json (v0.3.9) has no `engines` key; packages/unplugin-export-plugin/package.json (v1.2.16) has no `engines` key. The root manifest declares package.json:10 `"engines": {"node": ">=24.15.0"}`, and the sibling published packages tuff-cli/tuff-core/tuff-intelligence do declare `">=24.0.0"`.
failure_scenario: An external plugin author on Node 20 installs @talex-touch/utils with no warning, then hits the ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT/type-stripping failure at require time instead of a clear EBADENGINE message at install time. The same applies to unplugin-export-plugin, whose tsup build output targets modern Node.
recommendation: Add `"engines": {"node": ">=24.15.0"}` to all three published manifests (or the lowest version actually supported).

title: Four packages declare engines node >=24.0.0 while the workspace root requires >=24.15.0
summary: The published sub-packages advertise a Node floor 15 patch releases below what the repository itself mandates, so their declared support window is untested.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli/package.json:22 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:21 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-core/package.json:19 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-intelligence/package.json:45 `"node": ">=24.0.0"` versus root package.json:10 `"node": ">=24.15.0"`, .node-version `24.18.0`, and mise.toml:2 `node = "24.18.0"`.
failure_scenario: CI never runs on 24.0-24.14 (all workflows use `node-version-file: .node-version` = 24.18.0), so the advertised range is unverified. A consumer on Node 24.0 installs @talex-touch/tuff-cli without an EBADENGINE warning and can hit any 24.x behaviour change the code implicitly relies on.
recommendation: Raise all four to `>=24.15.0` to match the root engines declaration.

title: drizzle-kit is not installed anywhere; the documented db:generate/db:migrate scripts fail
summary: Two npm scripts and the drizzle config file depend on drizzle-kit, but it is declared in no manifest and has no entry in the lockfile.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:31 `"db:generate": "drizzle-kit generate",` :32 `"db:migrate": "drizzle-kit migrate",` and apps/core-app/drizzle.config.ts:1 `import type { Config } from 'drizzle-kit'`. `grep -n drizzle apps/core-app/package.json` shows only those two scripts plus :115 `"drizzle-orm": "^0.45.2"` — no drizzle-kit dependency. `grep -c drizzle-kit pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 0.
failure_scenario: `pnpm -F @talex-touch/core-app run db:generate` exits with 'drizzle-kit: command not found'. CLAUDE.md documents both commands as the supported way to create and apply migrations, so schema changes in src/main/db/schema.ts cannot be turned into migrations without a manual global install. drizzle.config.ts also fails to resolve its type import if it is ever added to a tsconfig include list.
recommendation: Add `drizzle-kit` (matching the drizzle-orm 0.45.x line) to apps/core-app devDependencies.

title: pnpm overrides force @sentry/electron onto 10.65.0 despite its exact 10.62.0 pins
summary: @sentry/electron 7.15.0 declares its Sentry sub-packages with exact (non-range) versions, signalling a matched-set requirement. Three targeted overrides push them a minor forward, which is exactly the kind of conflict overrides are supposed to surface rather than bury.
evidence: package.json:131-133 `"@sentry/electron>@sentry/browser": "10.65.0", "@sentry/electron>@sentry/core": "10.65.0", "@sentry/electron>@sentry/node": "10.65.0"`. node_modules/@sentry/electron/package.json declares `dependencies: {"@sentry/browser":"10.62.0","@sentry/core":"10.62.0","@sentry/node":"10.62.0"}` (exact pins) and `peerDependencies: {"@sentry/node-native":"10.62.0"}`. Installed tree: @sentry/electron 7.15.0 with @sentry/node, @sentry/core and @sentry/browser all at 10.65.0; @sentry/node-native is NOT INSTALLED.
failure_scenario: Sentry ships its JS SDK packages as a version-locked set; @sentry/electron's Electron-specific integrations are compiled against @sentry/core 10.62.0 internals (client, scope and transport plumbing that change between minors without a semver-major). Running them against 10.65.0 can break event enrichment or crash-report attachment silently at runtime. It also creates an unsatisfiable state for the optional @sentry/node-native peer, which demands exactly 10.62.0 while the rest of the stack is forced to 10.65.0.
recommendation: Drop the three overrides and upgrade @sentry/electron to a release that already depends on 10.65.0, so the matched set stays intact.

title: The npm `original-fs` shim defeats the ASAR-bypass fallback in build attestation
summary: attestation.ts requires 'original-fs' inside a try/catch that falls back to node:fs, expecting the require to fail outside Electron. Declaring the userland original-fs package — which is literally `module.exports=require('fs')` — makes that require always succeed and silently return plain fs.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:127 `"original-fs": "^1.2.0",`. node_modules/original-fs/index.js is one line: `'use strict';module.exports=require('fs');` and its own description reads 'Ensure that the correct module is loaded in a non-Electron environment.' apps/core-app/src/main/modules/build-verification/attestation.ts:109 `physicalFs = requireFromCurrentModule('original-fs') as typeof nodeFs` inside `try { ... } catch { physicalFs = nodeFs }`, feeding :117 `createReadStream` for :121 `hashFileSha256`.
failure_scenario: Electron's built-in original-fs wins inside the main process, so the intended ASAR bypass works there. But in any non-Electron Node context — the utility-process workers declared in apps/core-app/electron.vite.config.ts:209-221, or a plain `node out/main/...` run — the resolver now finds the npm shim instead of throwing, so the catch never fires and the attestation hashes bytes read *through* the ASAR layer rather than the raw archive. The integrity check then compares the wrong bytes without any error.
recommendation: Remove the original-fs dependency so the require genuinely fails outside Electron, or replace the try/catch with an explicit `process.versions.electron` check.

title: extension-loader uses session.loadExtension(), deprecated in Electron 41 in favour of ses.extensions
summary: The Chrome-extension loader calls a session API that Electron 41's own type definitions mark deprecated with a named replacement.
evidence: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/extension-loader.ts:74 `const loaded = await session.defaultSession.loadExtension(fullPath)`. node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:12907-12911 documents it as `**Deprecated:** Use the new ses.extensions.loadExtension API.` followed by `@deprecated` on `loadExtension(path: string, options?: LoadExtensionOptions)`. Electron 41.10.2 exposes the replacement namespace at electron.d.ts:13158 `readonly extensions: Extensions;`. The sibling calls session.removeExtension / getAllExtensions are deprecated in the same release (electron.d.ts:12932, :12791).
failure_scenario: Electron removes deprecated APIs on a two-major cadence, so this call is scheduled to disappear. When it does, ExtensionLoaderModule (module 4 in the documented boot order) throws `session.defaultSession.loadExtension is not a function` during startup and the whole module chain after it fails to initialise.
recommendation: Switch to `session.defaultSession.extensions.loadExtension(...)` (and the matching extensions.remove/getAllExtensions).

title: nuxt.config.ts hardcodes deep node_modules file paths into @panva/hkdf and next-auth internals
summary: Two build aliases point at specific files inside dependency packages, bypassing their exports maps and depending on both the internal dist layout and on hoisting placing them at those exact locations.
evidence: apps/nexus/nuxt.config.ts:47 `const hkdfCompatEntry = resolve(workspaceRoot, 'node_modules/@panva/hkdf/dist/node/cjs/index.js')` and :48 `const nextAuthCoreEntry = resolve(currentDir, 'node_modules/next-auth/core/index.js')`.
failure_scenario: The first path assumes @panva/hkdf keeps its dist/node/cjs layout (the root override pins it to 1.2.1 precisely because of this) AND that .npmrc:1 `shamefully-hoist=true` places it at the workspace root — under a strict pnpm layout the file is inside a .pnpm store path and the alias resolves to a non-existent file, so the Nuxt build fails with an unresolved alias. The second path is a next-auth v4-only internal; next-auth v5 removed the `core/` directory entirely, so any upgrade past 4.24.x breaks the build rather than producing a deprecation error.
recommendation: Resolve both via `import.meta.resolve` / `createRequire(...).resolve(<package specifier>)` instead of literal file paths, and stop reaching past the packages' exports maps.

title: apps/nexus package.json `imports` map points #auth into @sidebase/nuxt-auth's dist internals
summary: The subpath-imports map hard-codes a relative node_modules path into a dependency's compiled runtime, which is neither part of that package's public exports nor stable across its versions.
evidence: apps/nexus/package.json:9-10 `"#auth": "./node_modules/@sidebase/nuxt-auth/dist/runtime/server/services/index.js"` and `"#auth/*": "./node_modules/@sidebase/nuxt-auth/dist/runtime/server/services/*.js"`, against a dependency declared at :51 as `"@sidebase/nuxt-auth": "^0.9.4"` — a caret range on a pre-1.0 package.
failure_scenario: Node's `imports` field resolves relative to the package directory, so this only works when @sidebase/nuxt-auth is physically materialised at apps/nexus/node_modules (a consequence of .npmrc:1 shamefully-hoist=true). Under pnpm's default layout, or after any 0.9.x → 0.10 release that reorganises dist/runtime, every `#auth` import in the Nitro server routes fails to resolve and the API layer will not build.
recommendation: Use the alias the @sidebase/nuxt-auth Nuxt module itself registers, or map #auth through a local re-export file that imports the package by its public specifier.

title: Half the pnpm catalog is dead: 17 of 30 root catalog entries have zero `catalog:` references
summary: The catalog is meant to be the single source of version truth, but most entries are never referenced, and several of those unreferenced entries disagree with the literal versions the packages actually install.
evidence: Scanning every workspace package.json for `"<name>": "catalog:"`, these 17 root-catalog entries have 0 references: @auth/core (pnpm-workspace.yaml:35), @iconify-json/logos (:38), @langchain/anthropic (:39), @langchain/core (:40), @langchain/langgraph (:41), @langchain/openai (:42), @sidebase/nuxt-auth (:44), ai-elements-vue (:45), better-sqlite3 (:46), jsqr (:50), markdown-it (:52), next-auth (:54), nodemailer (:55), openapi-typescript (:57), qrcode (:58), theme-colors (:61), vue-sonner (:64). Three further pseudo-catalogs at :102-107 (`conflicts_next-auth_t4_24_14`, `conflicts_@langchain/langgraph_h0_4_9`, `conflicts_@langchain/openai_h0_4_9`) are likewise referenced by nothing.
failure_scenario: Contributors reading pnpm-workspace.yaml to answer 'what version of X does this repo use?' get wrong answers for langgraph (catalog ^0.2.74 vs installed ^0.4.9), openai (^0.3.17 vs ^0.4.9), next-auth (~4.21.1 vs ~4.24.14) and nodemailer (^9.0.3 vs not installed). Adopting `catalog:` for any of them — the documented convention — silently downgrades the dependency. The conflicts_ catalogs record known version conflicts that were never actually resolved.
recommendation: Delete the unreferenced entries and the conflicts_ catalogs, or convert the real consumers to `catalog:` and correct the versions.

title: tuffex build runs gulp-sass 5.1.0, which uses the Sass legacy JS API removed in Dart Sass 2.0
summary: The component library's style pipeline goes through gulp-sass, which still calls sass.render/renderSync — the legacy API Dart Sass deprecated and will delete in 2.0.
evidence: packages/tuffex/packages/script/build/index.ts:30 and :38 `.pipe(sass())`, driven by packages/tuffex/package.json:45 `"build": "node --loader ts-node/esm ./node_modules/gulp/bin/gulp.js -f packages/script/build/index.ts"`. node_modules/gulp-sass/index.js:145 `gulpSass.compiler.render(opts, ...)` and :158 `gulpSass.compiler.renderSync(opts)`. Verified with the installed sass@1.101.0: calling renderSync prints `DEPRECATION WARNING [legacy-js-api]: The legacy JS API is deprecated and will be removed in Dart Sass 2.0.0.`
failure_scenario: gulp-sass 5.1.0 has no modern-API path. When sass 2.0 ships, bumping the `sass: ^1.101.0` catalog entry (pnpm-workspace.yaml:59) breaks the tuffex build outright with 'sass.renderSync is not a function', taking down the component CSS that apps/core-app, apps/nexus and apps/tuff-analyse all consume from dist/es.
recommendation: Replace gulp-sass with a direct `sass.compile()` step (or a Vite/Rollup style pipeline) before sass 2.0 lands.

title: extract-file-icon@0.3.2 ships no prebuilds and pins node-addon-api to an exact 1.7.1
summary: A non-optional native dependency of the shipped app must compile C++ from source on every install, using a six-year-old exact node-addon-api pin that no override can lift.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:118 `"extract-file-icon": "^0.3.2",` (in `dependencies`, not `optionalDependencies`). The installed package contains only `binding.gyp build dist lib LICENSE package.json README.md` — no `prebuilds/` directory and no `binary` field — and declares `dependencies: {"node-addon-api":"1.7.1"}` (exact). It is listed in package.json:92 `onlyBuiltDependencies`, so pnpm runs node-gyp against the host toolchain; the sibling native package tuff-native uses node-addon-api ^7.1.1.
failure_scenario: Because it sits in `dependencies` rather than `optionalDependencies` (unlike uiohook-napi and @crosscopy/clipboard, which ship prebuilds), a missing C++ toolchain makes `pnpm install` fail outright for the whole workspace — on any dev machine without Xcode Command Line Tools / MSVC / build-essential, and on any CI image that trims build tools. The exact node-addon-api 1.7.1 pin also means the addon cannot pick up N-API header fixes; it is compiled against Node 24 headers here while the app runs Electron 41 (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 145 vs 137), which only survives because node-addon-api targets the ABI-stable N-API surface.
recommendation: Move it to optionalDependencies with a runtime guard (icon-worker.ts:68 already uses a dynamic import), or replace it with the in-house @talex-touch/tuff-native app-icon binding it already duplicates.

title: onlyBuiltDependencies is stale: 13 of 29 entries absent from the lockfile, fsevents missing
summary: The pnpm build-script allowlist still names packages that were removed from the repo long ago, while a native module that is actually installed is absent from it.
evidence: package.json:92 `"onlyBuiltDependencies": [ ... ]`. Checking each entry against pnpm-lock.yaml snapshots, these 13 have zero entries: @compodoc/compodoc, @google/genai, @nestjs/core, @parcel/watcher, @sentry/cli, @swc/core, browser-tabs-lock, core-js, get-windows, msgpackr-extract, puppeteer, simple-git-hooks, tesseract.js. Meanwhile fsevents@2.3.3 is installed (required by the chokidar 3.6.0 FSEvents backend aliased at apps/core-app/package.json:111 `"chokidar-fsevents": "npm:chokidar@3.6.0"`) but is not listed.
failure_scenario: The stale entries document a dependency set that no longer exists — notably `tesseract.js` and `get-windows`, whose jobs are now done by @talex-touch/tuff-native — so the file misleads anyone auditing which native builds the workspace permits. More concretely, any future native package that needs a build script but is not on the list is silently skipped by pnpm and fails at runtime rather than at install time.
recommendation: Prune the 13 dead entries and add fsevents so the allowlist reflects the packages actually built.

title: README claims MIT License but repo ships MPL-2.0
summary: Both READMEs state the project is MIT-licensed, while the LICENSE file is Mozilla Public License 2.0 and package.json declares MPL-2.0.
evidence: README.md:77 says 'This project is open-sourced under the **MIT License**.' — but LICENSE:1 is 'Mozilla Public License Version 2.0' and package.json:8 declares "license": "MPL-2.0 license". The badge on README.md:7 links to that same MPL-2.0 LICENSE file.
failure_scenario: A downstream consumer or company legal review reads the README, concludes the code is permissively MIT-licensed, and vendors/forks it without honouring MPL-2.0's file-level copyleft and source-disclosure obligations — a licensing violation created purely by the doc.
recommendation: Change both READMEs to MPL-2.0 (or fix LICENSE/package.json if MIT is the intent); the three sources must agree.

title: zh-CN README repeats the wrong MIT license claim
summary: The Chinese README makes the same incorrect MIT claim as the English one, so neither language surface tells a reader the real license.
evidence: README.zh-CN.md:100 says '本项目基于 **MIT 许可证** 开源。' — contradicted by LICENSE:1 'Mozilla Public License Version 2.0' and package.json:8 "license": "MPL-2.0 license".
failure_scenario: A Chinese-speaking contributor or integrator checks only README.zh-CN.md, believes MIT terms apply, and redistributes modified sources closed-source in violation of MPL-2.0.
recommendation: Update to MPL-2.0 in lockstep with README.md.

title: CLAUDE.md documents seven pnpm core:build* scripts that do not exist
summary: The 'Development Commands' section lists core:build, core:build:beta, core:build:snapshot, core:build:release and the three core:build:snapshot:<platform> variants; the root package.json defines none of them.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:9-17 lists '`pnpm core:build` - Build the main application for production' through '`pnpm core:build:snapshot:linux` - Build Linux snapshot'. The only core:* script in package.json is line 19 "core:dev". The real build scripts are unprefixed: package.json:23-35 define "build", "build:beta", "build:snapshot", "build:release", "build:snapshot:win|mac|linux".
failure_scenario: A developer or agent runs `pnpm core:build` as documented and gets 'Command "core:build" not found', with no hint that the working script is `pnpm build`.
recommendation: Rename the documented commands to the actual `pnpm build*` names (only `core:dev`/`nexus:dev` carry the app prefix).

title: CLAUDE.md documents pnpm docs:dev / docs:build for a docs app that was deleted
summary: A whole 'Documentation' command section points at scripts and an app directory that no longer exist anywhere in the repo.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:29-30: '`pnpm docs:dev` - Start documentation development server' / '`pnpm docs:build` - Build documentation'. Neither script exists in package.json (the doc site is now `nexus:dev`/`nexus:build`, package.json:20-21), and `apps/` contains only core-app, nexus, reverse-proxy-design and tuff-analyse — there is no apps/docs.
failure_scenario: Someone asked to update the docs site runs `pnpm docs:dev`, hits 'Command "docs:dev" not found', then looks for apps/docs/ and finds nothing, with no pointer to apps/nexus.
recommendation: Replace the section with `pnpm nexus:dev` / `pnpm nexus:build` and point at apps/nexus.

title: CLAUDE.md monorepo description cites apps/docs and '7 plugin packages'
summary: The one-line map of the monorepo names a directory that does not exist and undercounts plugins by more than 3x.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:43: 'This is a pnpm workspace monorepo with the main application in `apps/core-app/`, utility packages in `packages/`, extracted plugins in `plugins/` (7 independent plugin packages), and documentation in `apps/docs/`.' Reality: `ls apps/` returns core-app, nexus, reverse-proxy-design, tuff-analyse (no docs); `ls -1d plugins/*/ | wc -l` returns 24.
failure_scenario: A newcomer forms a mental model with a docs app that doesn't exist and 7 plugins, then cannot locate the doc site or the other 17 plugin directories when asked to touch either.
recommendation: Say 24 plugin directories under plugins/, and name apps/nexus as the docs+dashboard app.

title: CLAUDE.md tech stack says Electron 40 / Node 22.16 but engines require Node >=24.15
summary: The stated runtime baseline is two majors behind for Electron and one major behind for Node, and the Node claim is below the hard `engines` floor so following it makes install fail.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:46 '- **Electron**: 40.0.0+ with Node.js 22.16.0+' and CLAUDE.md:373-374 '- Node.js version: 22.16.0+ (enforced by pnpm preinstall hook and Volta)' / '- Uses Electron 40.0.0+ with Vue 3.5.27+'. package.json:9-11 declares "engines": { "node": ">=24.15.0" }, package.json:64 "electron": "^41.10.1", package.json:88-90 "volta": { "node": "24.18.0" }, and .node-version pins the same 24 line.
failure_scenario: A contributor provisions Node 22.16 because CLAUDE.md says it is the supported floor, then `pnpm install` fails the engines check on every workspace package before any code is written.
recommendation: State Node >=24.15.0 and Electron 41.x, sourced from package.json engines/dependencies.

title: CLAUDE.md says the preinstall hook enforces the Node version; it only enforces pnpm
summary: The Development Notes attribute Node-version enforcement to the pnpm preinstall hook, which actually only blocks non-pnpm package managers.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:373 '- Node.js version: 22.16.0+ (enforced by pnpm preinstall hook and Volta)'. package.json:14 defines "preinstall": "npx only-allow pnpm" — only-allow checks the package manager, not the Node version. Node is gated by "engines" (package.json:9-11), volta (:88-90) and .node-version.
failure_scenario: A maintainer debugging why a wrong-Node contributor got through inspects the preinstall hook expecting a version check, finds only-allow, and wastes time before looking at engines.
recommendation: Attribute the gate to package.json engines + volta + .node-version.

title: CLAUDE.md module loading order lists 15 modules; startup loads 39 in a different order
summary: The documented startup sequence is missing 24 modules, names one module that does not exist, and gets the relative order of the ones it does list wrong.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:74: '1. DatabaseModule → 2. StorageModule → 3. ShortcutModule → 4. ExtensionLoaderModule → 5. CommonChannelModule → 6. PluginModule → 7. PluginLogModule → 8. CoreBoxModule → 9. TrayHolderModule → 10. AddonOpenerModule → 11. ClipboardModule → 12. TuffDashboardModule → 13. FileSystemWatcher → 14. FileProtocolModule → 15. TerminalModule'. apps/core-app/src/main/index.ts:171-210 defines foregroundModulesToLoad with 37 entries (databaseModule, conversationModule, toolGatewayModule, storageModule, fileProtocolModule, shortcutModule, commonChannelModule, trayManagerModule, ... downloadCenterModule) and index.ts:212 deferredModulesToLoad = [extensionLoaderModule, FileSystemWatcher]. There is no 'TrayHolderModule' — it is trayManagerModule and loads 8th, not 9th; fileProtocolModule is 5th, not 14th; extensionLoaderModule is deferred, not 4th.
failure_scenario: A developer adding a module that must run after permissions/auth uses the documented 15-step order to pick an insertion point, lands it before permissionModule/authModule (index.ts:184,196) which the doc never mentions, and gets an ordering bug that only reproduces at startup.
recommendation: Either regenerate the list from index.ts:171-212 or replace it with a pointer to that array as the single source of truth.

title: CLAUDE.md channel API block mixes main-process and renderer signatures
summary: The six "Key APIs" are presented as one surface, but they come from two different classes with incompatible signatures, and sendTo as written matches neither.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:245-254 lists, under one "Key APIs" block: 'regChannel(type: ChannelType, eventName: string, callback)', 'send(eventName: string, arg?: any)', 'sendTo(window: BrowserWindow, eventName: string, arg?: any)', 'sendPlugin(pluginName, eventName, arg?)', 'requestKey(name)', 'revokeKey(key)'. Main process (apps/core-app/src/main/core/channel-core.ts): regChannel matches (:570), but send is 'send(type: ChannelType, eventName: string, arg: unknown)' (:800) and sendTo is 'sendTo(win, type: ChannelType, eventName, arg)' (:772-777) — both require a ChannelType the doc omits. Renderer (apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/modules/channel/channel-core.ts): send matches (:205) but regChannel takes no ChannelType (:177), and the class has no sendTo, sendPlugin, requestKey or revokeKey at all. So the documented sendTo(window, eventName, arg) signature exists on neither side.
failure_scenario: A main-process developer copies `channel.send('my-event', payload)` from the doc; TypeScript rejects it because the first argument must be a ChannelType. A renderer developer copies `regChannel(ChannelType.MAIN, 'evt', cb)` and passes the ChannelType where the event name is expected, silently registering a handler under the wrong key that never fires.
recommendation: Split the block into main-process and renderer subsections with each class's real signatures, and drop the sendTo form that matches neither.

title: CLAUDE.md storage channel names (storage:get/save/delete) exist nowhere in the codebase
summary: All five documented storage IPC channel names are absent from the source; the real storage transport uses a different namespace shape.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:302-303: '- Main process: `storage:get`, `storage:save`, `storage:delete`' and '- Plugin process: `plugin:storage:get-item`, `plugin:storage:set-item`'. A repo-wide grep for these literals over apps/, packages/ and plugins/ returns zero source hits. The channels that do exist are e.g. 'storage:sqlite:query' (apps/core-app/src/main/modules/plugin/services/plugin-storage-transport-service.ts:377), 'storage:plugin:secret' (:383) and 'storage:plugin:file' (:449).
failure_scenario: A plugin or renderer author wires `storage:get` per the doc; the channel has no registered handler, so the call resolves to nothing or trips the missing-handler policy, and the developer cannot find the name anywhere in the repo to debug it.
recommendation: Regenerate the channel list from plugin-storage-transport-service.ts and the storage module's actual registrations.

title: CLAUDE.md plugin manifest example omits sdkapi, so a copied manifest is hard-blocked at load
summary: The canonical manifest example has no sdkapi and no category; the loader's hard-cut gate rejects a manifest with undefined sdkapi outright, and category is mandatory for every currently supported sdkapi.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:137-161 shows the full 'Plugin Manifest Example' with id/name/version/features/dev and no sdkapi or category. apps/core-app/src/main/modules/plugin/sdkapi-hard-cut-gate.ts:35-42 returns '{ blocked: true, reason: 'missing-sdkapi' }' when declaredSdkapi === undefined, and plugin-loaders.ts:278-299 turns that into setLoadState('load_failed'). plugin-loaders.ts:302-324 additionally errors with CATEGORY_MISSING when resolvedSdkapi >= 260114. A real manifest (plugins/touch-intelligence/manifest.json:5-6) declares "sdkapi": 260713 and "category": "ai".
failure_scenario: A plugin author copies the documented manifest verbatim; the plugin never loads and surfaces only a PLUGIN_SDK_BLOCKED error about a field the documentation never mentioned.
recommendation: Add "sdkapi" (current value per packages/utils/plugin/sdk-version.ts) and "category" to the example, and note both are load-blocking.

title: CLAUDE.md lists a non-existent touch-intelligence-actions plugin
summary: One of the seven named 'extracted plugins' does not exist under plugins/; the AI plugin directory is touch-intelligence.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:117: '- `touch-intelligence-actions` - AI intelligence actions'. `ls plugins/` has no touch-intelligence-actions; the AI plugin is plugins/touch-intelligence (manifest.json:2-3 "id": "com.tuffex.intelligence", "name": "touch-intelligence"). The other six names in the list do resolve.
failure_scenario: A developer told to modify the AI actions plugin runs `cd plugins/touch-intelligence-actions` and gets 'no such file or directory', with no clue the directory was renamed.
recommendation: Correct the entry to touch-intelligence.

title: apps/core-app README calls the repository LICENSE an MIT License
summary: A third doc surface mislabels the repository license, and it links directly to the MPL-2.0 file while calling it MIT.
evidence: apps/core-app/README.md:73: 'CoreApp is distributed under the repository [MIT License](../../LICENSE).' The link target LICENSE:1 reads 'Mozilla Public License Version 2.0', and apps/core-app/package.json declares "license": "MPL-2.0 license". (packages/tuffex ships its own genuine MIT LICENSE, so the confusion is plausible but the root claim is still wrong.)
failure_scenario: Someone evaluating whether they can embed CoreApp in a proprietary product reads this line, clicks through assuming MIT, and misreads the MPL text — or does not click at all and ships a non-compliant integration.
recommendation: Say MPL-2.0, matching LICENSE and apps/core-app/package.json.

title: License badge links point at a 'main' branch that does not exist
summary: The license badges in both READMEs and both contribution guides link to /blob/main/LICENSE, but the repository's only branch on origin is master, so every one of those links 404s.
evidence: README.md:7 '[![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/talex-touch/tuff?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/talex-touch/tuff/blob/main/LICENSE)' — identical at README.zh-CN.md:10, .github/docs/contribution/CONTRIBUTING.md:8 and CONTRIBUTING_zh.md:8. `git ls-remote --heads origin main master` returns only 'refs/heads/master', and origin/HEAD points to origin/master.
failure_scenario: A reader clicks the license badge to read the actual terms and lands on GitHub's 404 page, so the one link that could have corrected the wrong MIT claim in the prose is itself dead.
recommendation: Use /blob/master/LICENSE or a branch-less /blob/HEAD/LICENSE link.

title: CONTRIBUTING recommends commit types add/upd that commitlint rejects
summary: The commit-message guide tells contributors to use `add(...)` and `upd(...)`, but neither type is in the commitlint type-enum, and the husky commit-msg hook enforces it.
evidence: .github/docs/contribution/CONTRIBUTING.md:57-58: '- add(xxx): message' and '- upd(xxx): message (Update dependencies versions)'. commitlint.config.cts:4-29 defines 'type-enum' at severity 2 with the allowed list change, update, feat, fix, docs, style, ref, test, chore, revert, merge, sync, build, ci, perf, wf, types, release, config, sec, upg — no 'add', and 'upd' is spelled 'update'/'upg'. .husky/commit-msg runs 'pnpm exec commitlint --config "commitlint.config.cts" --edit "$1"' on every commit. CONTRIBUTING_zh.md:56-57 repeats both.
failure_scenario: A first-time contributor writes `add(search): new provider` exactly as documented; the commit-msg hook aborts the commit with a type-enum error listing types the guide never mentioned, and they have to reverse-engineer the real list from the config.
recommendation: Replace add/upd with the real enum values (feat/update/upg) or generate the list from commitlint.config.cts.

title: CONTRIBUTING points to commitlint.config.js; the file is commitlint.config.cts
summary: The escape hatch for finding the authoritative commit-type list names a file extension that does not exist in the repo.
evidence: .github/docs/contribution/CONTRIBUTING.md:60: '- More see `commitlint.config.js`' (CONTRIBUTING_zh.md:59 '更多请参考 `commitlint.config.js`'). The repository root contains commitlint.config.cts only, and .husky/commit-msg explicitly passes '--config "commitlint.config.cts"'.
failure_scenario: A contributor whose commit was rejected opens the guide, looks for commitlint.config.js, does not find it, and gives up on discovering the allowed types.
recommendation: Point to commitlint.config.cts.

title: CONTRIBUTING project-structure tree names three directories that do not exist
summary: The onboarding tree lists apps/core, apps/docs and packages/components; the real directories are apps/core-app, apps/nexus and packages/tuffex.
evidence: .github/docs/contribution/CONTRIBUTING.md:75-80 shows '├── apps: (Main applications)' / '├──── core: (Electron application)' / '├──── docs: (Document application)' / '├── packages: (Assistant packages)' / '├──── components: (Tuff components)'. Actual: apps/ holds core-app, nexus, reverse-proxy-design, tuff-analyse (no core, no docs); packages/ holds tuffex (the component library) with no components directory. CONTRIBUTING_zh.md:74-77 mirrors the same tree.
failure_scenario: A new contributor following the tree runs `cd apps/core` or `cd packages/components`, gets 'no such file or directory', and has to guess which of tuffex/nexus corresponds to which entry.
recommendation: Regenerate the tree from the real apps/ and packages/ listings.

title: CONTRIBUTING badges use the pre-rename repo slug and hardcode release 1.2.0
summary: The contribution guide's badges still target github.com/talex-touch/talex-touch and advertise static versions 1.2.0 / 2.1.0, while the repo is talex-touch/tuff at 2.4.14-beta.2.
evidence: .github/docs/contribution/CONTRIBUTING.md:7-10 includes 'https://img.shields.io/github/issues/talex-touch/talex-touch' and the static badges 'https://img.shields.io/badge/release-1.2.0-42B883' and 'https://img.shields.io/badge/dev-2.1.0-64391A'. `git remote -v` resolves origin to https://github.com/talex-touch/tuff.git, and package.json:4 is "version": "2.4.14-beta.2". The root README.md:6-8 already uses the talex-touch/tuff slug.
failure_scenario: A contributor reads the guide and believes the current release is 1.2.0 and dev is 2.1.0 — off by more than a major version — and files bug reports against versions that have not shipped in years.
recommendation: Repoint the badges at talex-touch/tuff and use dynamic release badges instead of hardcoded versions.

title: TuffEx README claims 102 export modules; components.ts exports 126
summary: The component inventory is 24 modules short of the export entry it cites as the source of truth, and omits the entire AI-surface family added since.
evidence: packages/tuffex/README.md:70: 'Current source-of-truth export modules: **102**.' and README.md:82 names the source: '- Export entry: `packages/components/src/components.ts`'. That file contains 126 `export * from './<module>/index'` lines. Modules present in components.ts but absent from the README's seven category lists (README.md:72-78) include ai-elements, attachment-tray, chain-of-thought, conversation-stream, stream-markdown, thinking-orb, tool-call-card, reasoning-disclosure, sources, suggestion-chips, message-actions, context-indicator, copy-button, divider, kbd, textarea, number-input, icon-button, os-icon, resize-box, markdown-editor and flat-dropdown.
failure_scenario: A plugin developer scanning the inventory for an AI chat surface concludes TuffEx only ships `chat` and hand-rolls a streaming markdown/tool-call UI, unaware that stream-markdown, conversation-stream and tool-call-card already exist and are exported.
recommendation: Generate the count and category lists from components.ts, or drop the count and link to the generated export list.

title: Nexus README says the dev server runs on port 3000; it is pinned to 3200
summary: The documented local URL does not match the port the dev script hardcodes.
evidence: apps/nexus/README.md:13-17 shows '```bash\npnpm run dev\n```' followed by 'The site will be available at `http://localhost:3000`.' apps/nexus/package.json defines "dev": "NUXT_USE_CLOUDFLARE_DEV=true CLOUDFLARE_DEV_ENVIRONMENT=preview nuxt dev --port 3200".
failure_scenario: A developer starts the docs site, opens http://localhost:3000 as instructed, sees connection refused, and assumes the build is broken rather than checking the terminal for the real port.
recommendation: State port 3200, or read it from the dev script.

title: CLAUDE.md 'Key File Locations' lists four files that no longer exist
summary: Four of the eleven entries in the key-file index, plus two duplicate links earlier in the doc, point at paths that were refactored away.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:404 '- Core app logic: [apps/core-app/src/main/core/touch-core.ts](...)', :406 '- Plugin system: [.../modules/plugin/plugin-provider.ts](...)', :407 '- CoreBox launcher: [.../modules/box-tool/core-box.ts](...)', :409 '- Storage module: [.../modules/storage/storage-provider.ts](...)' — none of the four files exist. CLAUDE.md:64-65 repeat the core-box.ts and plugin-provider.ts links. Reality: src/main/core/ contains touch-app.ts (no touch-core.ts); box-tool/core-box is now a directory, not a file; modules/plugin/ has plugin-module.ts / plugin-loaders.ts / plugin-resolver.ts but no plugin-provider.ts; modules/storage/ has index.ts and app-config-repository.ts but no storage-provider.ts. The other seven entries (index.ts, module-manager.ts, channel-core.ts, permission/, transport/, plugins/, renderer main.ts) do resolve.
failure_scenario: An agent or developer told to 'start from the file locations in CLAUDE.md' opens four dead paths in a row and has to re-derive the module layout by hand — exactly what the index exists to prevent.
recommendation: Repoint to touch-app.ts, modules/plugin/plugin-module.ts, modules/box-tool/core-box/ and modules/storage/index.ts.

title: CLAUDE.md says @talex-touch/utils is v1.0.23; it is v1.0.50
summary: The published version pinned in the shared-utilities section is 27 patch releases behind the workspace manifest.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:307: '**`@talex-touch/utils`** (npm package v1.0.23) provides shared types and utilities'. packages/utils/package.json declares "version": "1.0.50".
failure_scenario: An external plugin developer pins "@talex-touch/utils": "1.0.23" from the doc and misses every API added since — including the transport domain SDKs the same section advertises.
recommendation: Drop the hardcoded version and point at packages/utils/package.json.

title: CLAUDE.md technology-stack versions drifted across seven dependencies
summary: Beyond the Electron/Node baseline, most pinned versions in the tech-stack block no longer match the manifests or the workspace catalog.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:49-52 claims 'Vite 7.3.1, Electron-Builder 26.4.0', 'UnoCSS 66.6.0, SASS 1.97.2', 'Drizzle ORM 0.44.7 with LibSQL 0.15.15', 'VueUse 14.1.0, Dayjs 1.11.19'. Actual: package.json:85 vite ^7.3.6 (and override 7.3.6 at :190); apps/core-app/package.json electron-builder ^26.15.3, drizzle-orm ^0.45.2, @libsql/client ^0.17.4, dayjs ^1.11.21; pnpm-workspace.yaml:81 unocss ^66.7.5, :59 sass ^1.101.0, :96 '@vueuse/core' ^14.3.0. Only electron-vite 4.0.1, vue-router 4.6.4, pinia 3.0.4, typescript 5.9.3, xterm 5.3.0 and log4js 6.9.1 still match.
failure_scenario: A developer resolving a dependency conflict trusts the doc's LibSQL 0.15.x / Drizzle 0.44.x pairing, reads changelogs for the wrong minor range, and misdiagnoses a migration or query-builder behaviour change that landed in 0.45/0.17.
recommendation: Replace the pinned numbers with a pointer to package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml catalog, as the README's prerequisites section already does.

title: CLAUDE.md BaseModule snippet omits the generic and the required protected constructor
summary: The documented base-class shape has no type parameter and no constructor, so a subclass written against it does not compile and has no module key.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:93-99 shows 'abstract class BaseModule {' with only onInit/onDestroy/created/start/stop and un-parameterised contexts. apps/core-app/src/main/modules/abstract-base-module.ts:27 is 'export abstract class BaseModule<E = TalexEvents> implements TalexTouch.IModule<E>' and :36 declares 'protected constructor(key: ModuleKey, file?: ModuleFileConfig, env?: ModuleEnvFlag)' which sets 'this.name = key' (:37) — the ModuleKey the doc itself calls the singleton symbol key at CLAUDE.md:104. All five lifecycle contexts are generic (ModuleInitContext<E> etc.).
failure_scenario: A developer writes `class MyModule extends BaseModule { onInit() {} onDestroy() {} }` from the snippet; TypeScript rejects the implicit `super()` (expected 1-3 arguments) and, once that is patched blindly, the module has no name so ModuleManager cannot register it as a singleton.
recommendation: Show the real signature including the protected constructor and the ModuleKey argument, or show a minimal working subclass.

title: Both READMEs state the stable baseline is 2.4.13; the manifests say 2.4.14-beta.2
summary: The release-status paragraph names a version and claims it is resolved from the package manifests, but the manifests it cites hold a different version.
evidence: README.md:19: 'The repository's stable baseline is `2.4.13`, resolved from the matching [root package manifest](./package.json) and [CoreApp package manifest](./apps/core-app/package.json).' README.zh-CN.md:18 repeats it: '仓库当前稳定基线为 `2.4.13`，由一致的[根目录 package manifest]...确定。' Both manifests declare "version": "2.4.14-beta.2" (package.json:4, apps/core-app/package.json).
failure_scenario: A reader verifying the claim opens package.json as instructed, sees 2.4.14-beta.2, and cannot tell whether the README is stale or the repo is mid-release — the sentence is self-refuting because it names its own source.
recommendation: Either drop the number and keep only the pointer to the manifests, or wire it into the version-sync script (scripts/version-sync.mjs).

title: ROADMAP header pins v2.4.13 against a manifest that reads 2.4.14-beta.2
summary: The roadmap's current-version table cites apps/core-app/package.json but states a version that file no longer contains — the same anti-pattern its own docs index forbids.
evidence: ROADMAP.md:6 '## 🎯 当前版本：v2.4.13' and ROADMAP.md:10 '| CoreApp 版本 | `2.4.13`（`apps/core-app/package.json`） |'. apps/core-app/package.json declares "version": "2.4.14-beta.2". docs/INDEX.md:67 explicitly rules this out: '长期文档不得固化本地 `HEAD`、dirty worktree、当前分支或可从 `package.json` 读取的版本'. The adjacent Node/pnpm/Electron rows (ROADMAP.md:11-13) are correct.
failure_scenario: Someone triaging whether a fix shipped reads 'current version v2.4.13', assumes 2.4.14 work has not started, and duplicates or mis-targets a backport.
recommendation: Remove the hardcoded version row per the docs/INDEX.md rule and link to the manifest.

title: ROADMAP links three archived tasks as active with in_progress/planning status
summary: Three rows of the active-task table link to .trellis/tasks/<id>/prd.md paths that were moved to the archive, so the links 404 and the stated statuses are wrong.
evidence: ROADMAP.md:64 '| [batch-commit-release-v2-4-14-beta-1](.trellis/tasks/07-27-batch-commit-release-v2-4-14-beta-1/prd.md) | P1 | 🔄 planning [1/2] |', :65 the same for 07-27-release-v2-4-14-beta-1 ('planning'), :83 '| [fix-file-index-update-redaction-476](.trellis/tasks/07-30-fix-file-index-update-redaction-476/prd.md) | P2 | 🔄 in_progress |'. All three directories now live under .trellis/tasks/archive/ and are absent from .trellis/tasks/; the other 24 rows resolve.
failure_scenario: A maintainer picking up 'in_progress' work clicks fix-file-index-update-redaction-476, gets a dead path, and cannot tell whether the task was completed, renamed or lost.
recommendation: Drop archived rows from the active table (or link into .trellis/tasks/archive/<month>/).

title: ROADMAP calls its 27-row table the full active-task panorama; 63 tasks are active
summary: The heading promises a complete view of active Trellis tasks, but more than half of them — every task created since 2026-07-31 — are missing.
evidence: ROADMAP.md:53: '## 📁 活跃 Trellis 任务全景（27 个）'. `.trellis/tasks/` currently holds 63 task directories excluding archive/ and README.md; the table's newest entry is dated 07-30 while 30+ tasks dated 07-28 through 08-05 (e.g. 08-05-search-audit-remediation, 08-05-reco-signal-substrate, 08-04-settings-rewrite, 07-29-screenshot-*) have no row. ROADMAP.md:87 does offer the escape hatch '完整列表 → `python3 .trellis/scripts/task.py list`'.
failure_scenario: A contributor checking whether work on the recommendation engine or the screenshot suite is already claimed reads the 'panorama', sees nothing, and starts a duplicate task.
recommendation: Either regenerate the table from task.py or relabel it as a P0/P1 excerpt rather than 全景.

title: intelligence-uikit README documents a /conversation subpath and symbols that do not exist
summary: The documented compatibility entry point is not in the package's exports map, and neither of the two symbols it imports exists anywhere in the source.
evidence: packages/intelligence-uikit/README.md:26-31 shows 'import { mapAIChatBlocksToAiBlocks, TxAIConversation, } from "@talex-touch/intelligence-uikit/conversation"', and README.md:58 claims the package '提供 `@talex-touch/intelligence-uikit`、`@talex-touch/intelligence-uikit/conversation`、`@talex-touch/intelligence-uikit/style.css`'. packages/intelligence-uikit/package.json's exports map contains only "." and "./style.css" with no wildcard, so ./conversation is not a resolvable subpath. A repo-wide grep finds 'mapAIChatBlocksToAiBlocks' only inside a quoted playground code sample (src/playground/usePlaygroundState.ts:245) and finds zero occurrences of 'TxAIConversation' — the real component is TxAiConversation (src/components/conversation/TxAiConversation.vue:7), lowercase i.
failure_scenario: A developer copies the compatibility snippet and the bundler fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for the subpath; after rewriting it to the root entry the build still fails because mapAIChatBlocksToAiBlocks is not exported and TxAIConversation is not a real name.
recommendation: Delete the block or add a real ./conversation export and the missing symbols; at minimum fix the TxAiConversation casing.

title: Docs call DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED a default-off safety gate; code defaults it ON
summary: Every doc surface states the search-index split flag defaults off and warns that enabling it early causes silent data loss, but the runtime flag has defaulted to true since 2026-08-05 and no doc was updated.
evidence: docs/plan-prd/TODO.md:13, under the heading 'Non-negotiable safety gates': '- `DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED` / `TUFF_DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED` defaults **off**. Enabling it before all named 2d/2e writes migrate causes provider writes to land in `database.db` while reads use `search-index.db`: **silent data loss**.' The code is apps/core-app/src/main/db/runtime-flags.ts:26: 'export const DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED = parseEnvBoolean('TUFF_DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED', true)' — parseEnvBoolean's second argument is the default (runtime-flags.ts:3-14), and the comment at :20 states 'Default ON since 2026-08-05'. The same default-off claim appears at ROADMAP.md:47 ('默认 **off**，开启前必须有 flag-on app run evidence'), ROADMAP.md:168 ('🔴 默认 off，待 evidence') and docs/engineering/reports/maintenance-audit-2026-08-05.md:14 ('默认关闭').
failure_scenario: An engineer verifying the safety gate before a release reads 'defaults off' and ships without checking; the split topology is already live for every user, and nobody re-runs the flag-on acceptance the same paragraph declares mandatory. Conversely, someone trying to reproduce a bug in the shared-file topology assumes no env var is needed and cannot reproduce.
recommendation: Update TODO.md, ROADMAP.md:47/168 and the maintenance-audit index to state default-on plus the TUFF_DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED=0 kill switch, or revert the default if the evidence gate is genuinely unmet.

title: search-engine README says the split flag is default-off and migration incomplete
summary: The module-level README a search engineer reads first states the opposite of the shipped default and contradicts the code comment about migration status.
evidence: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/box-tool/search-engine/README.md:29-33: '`TUFF_DB_SEARCH_SPLIT_ENABLED` 当前默认关闭。启用后 search-index worker 使用独立的 `search-index.db`，但目录中已经存在 split 相关适配并不表示所有写路径已经迁移完成 ... 在剩余 writer、首次全量重建、回滚和真实 app-run 证据完成前，不应把该开关描述为生产默认能力。' apps/core-app/src/main/db/runtime-flags.ts:26 defaults the flag to true, and its comment (:20-23) claims exactly the opposite state: 'Default ON since 2026-08-05, validated by app runs (schema parity fixups, bootstrap reindex, 2d.3 write-path migration all landed; V2 run showed zero BUSY/FK).'
failure_scenario: A developer adding a new index writer reads this README, believes writes still go to the shared database.db by default, and skips the search-index.db worker ownership rules — landing writes in the wrong file for every user running the default configuration.
recommendation: Reconcile the README with runtime-flags.ts:20-26; whichever side is stale, both must state the same default and migration status.

title: English README omits the plugin-management policy and cross-platform sections the zh README carries
summary: Two substantive sections exist only in the Chinese README, so English readers never see the documented plugin install/uninstall behaviour or the cross-platform support caveat.
evidence: README.zh-CN.md:75-78 has a '### 插件管理策略' section ('官方市场下载的插件会在安装阶段自动关闭 manifest 中的 `dev` 入口，避免误连开发服务器。' / '每个插件的来源都会记录在数据库里，卸载时会连同插件目录与数据缓存一并清理。') and README.zh-CN.md:30-32 has '## 🖇️ 跨平台支持'. Neither section has any counterpart in README.md, whose 'Rich Functionality' list ends at line 55 and jumps straight to 'Simple and Easy-to-Use Operations' at :57. Conversely README.md:23-28 'Highlights' has no zh counterpart.
failure_scenario: An English-speaking plugin author does not learn that installing from the marketplace disables their manifest `dev` entry, and spends time debugging why their plugin stopped connecting to the local dev server after a marketplace install.
recommendation: Mirror the two zh-only sections into README.md (and Highlights into the zh file), or move shared factual content into one included fragment.

title: CLAUDE.md TalexEvents block shows 8 of 33 events and hides that it is a string enum
summary: The event-system section presents an eight-member value-less enum as the application event surface; the real enum has 33 string-valued members covering whole domains the doc never mentions.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:273-283 shows 'enum TalexEvents { APP_READY, APP_START, APP_SECONDARY_LAUNCH, ALL_MODULES_LOADED, BEFORE_APP_QUIT, WILL_QUIT, WINDOW_ALL_CLOSED, PLUGIN_STORAGE_UPDATED }'. apps/core-app/src/main/core/eventbus/touch-event.ts:17 declares 'export enum TalexEvents' with 33 members, all string-valued (e.g. 'APP_READY = 'app-ready''), including file-system (FILE_ADDED, FILE_CHANGED, FILE_UNLINKED, DIRECTORY_ADDED, FILE_WATCH_ROOT_RECOVERED), clipboard (CLIPBOARD_CHANGE), window (WINDOW_HIDDEN/SHOWN, COREBOX_WINDOW_HIDDEN/SHOWN), permission (PERMISSION_GRANTED/REVOKED), download, update, language and search-engine events. The eight listed names all exist.
failure_scenario: A developer needing to react to clipboard changes or file-index events reads this as the complete event surface, concludes TouchEventBus does not expose them, and hand-rolls a duplicate watcher instead of subscribing to CLIPBOARD_CHANGE or FILE_CHANGED.
recommendation: Mark the list as an excerpt and link to touch-event.ts:17, and show the string values so the enum's shape is clear.

title: TuffEx zh README repeats the stale 102 count and drops three sections
summary: The Chinese TuffEx README carries the same 24-module undercount as the English one and is missing its Integration, Contributing and License sections.
evidence: packages/tuffex/README_ZHCN.md:70: '当前源码导出模块总数：**102**。' — packages/tuffex/packages/components/src/components.ts contains 126 `export * from './<module>/index'` lines. Section-header comparison: README.md has 9 '## ' sections ending with 'Integration with Tuff' (:109), 'Contributing' (:113) and 'License' (:119); README_ZHCN.md has only 6, ending at '## 开发' (:96).
failure_scenario: A Chinese-reading contributor gets the same wrong inventory as the English reader, and additionally has no license or contribution pointer in the file they are reading.
recommendation: Regenerate the count from components.ts and mirror the three trailing sections.

title: Aux DB migration copies hot tables positionally, shifting ocr_jobs/plugin_analytics columns
summary: migrateHotTablesToAux() copies each hot table with `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO <t> SELECT * FROM coredb.<t>`, which is positional. The aux DDL in ensureAuxTables() declares columns in a different physical order than the primary file for two tables, because the primary got those columns via later ALTER TABLE (appended at the end) while the aux CREATE TABLE places them mid-list.
failure_scenario: Primary physical order is ocr_jobs(..., last_error, payload_hash, meta, queued_at, started_at, finished_at, next_retry_at) — next_retry_at was appended by migration 0008_damp_living_mummy.sql. On first launch with TUFF_DB_AUX_ENABLED, every ocr_jobs row is copied shifted by one: payload_hash lands in next_retry_at, meta in payload_hash, queued_at in meta, started_at in queued_at (NOT NULL -> the row is silently dropped by OR IGNORE when started_at is NULL). plugin_analytics is identical: plugin_version was appended by 0016_hidden_sunfire.sql, so feature_id lands in plugin_version, ..., and plugin_version lands in the NOT NULL timestamp column. The verification only logs `Aux migration verification mismatch` (line 962) and still calls markAuxMigrationCompleted(), so the corruption is permanent — the copy never re-runs.
recommendation: Enumerate columns explicitly (INSERT INTO t (cols...) SELECT cols... FROM coredb.t) or read the source column list from pragma_table_info and build the projection; treat a count mismatch as a failure instead of a warning.

title: saveConversation deletes all messages then re-inserts outside a transaction
summary: The replace-all write deletes every message row for a thread and then inserts the new set as two separate statements inside one scheduled task. scheduleDbWrite only serializes the task against other scheduled writes — it is not a transaction — so a failure of the insert leaves the thread permanently empty.
failure_scenario: The renderer sends a thread containing two messages with the same id (a retry that reuses an id, or a duplicated array after a stream restart). The DELETE succeeds, the multi-row INSERT aborts on the primary-key conflict, and the scheduled task rejects. conversations still has the row but every message is gone: the UI keeps showing the thread from memory, and on the next launch the conversation opens empty. The same happens for any mid-write failure (disk full, SQLITE_BUSY that outlives the retry budget).
recommendation: Wrap the delete + insert in db.transaction() so the delete rolls back with the insert.

title: 'duplicate column name: provider_id' migration catch skips every post-migrate ensure* fixup
summary: The five schema fixups that run after migrate() live inside the same try block as migrate(). When migrate() throws the tolerated 'duplicate column name: provider_id' error, the catch only logs a warning and execution continues past the whole block, so none of the fixups ever run on that launch.
failure_scenario: ensureKeywordMappingsProviderColumn() at line 1217 adds provider_id before migrate() runs; if a pending generated migration also adds it, migrate() throws the duplicate-column error. The app then starts with item_time_stats / recommendation_cache / analytics_snapshots missing and without idx_query_completions_prefix, idx_embeddings_source, idx_usage_logs_action_ts — every recommendation and analytics write fails at runtime with 'no such table', and completion queries fall back to full scans.
recommendation: Move the ensure* calls out of the migrate() try block (or into a finally) so a tolerated migrate failure still runs them.

title: Terminal child processes are never reaped when their renderer goes away
summary: create() spawns a child process keyed by a generated id and only removes it on 'close', 'error', or an explicit kill message. Nothing watches the requesting WebContents, so a renderer reload/close orphans the process for the lifetime of the app and the id needed to kill it is lost with the renderer.
failure_scenario: A user opens the terminal panel, runs a long-lived command (e.g. `tail -f`), then closes or reloads the window. sendToSender() short-circuits on sender.isDestroyed() so output is discarded, but the child keeps running and holding its pipes; this.processes grows with one dead-but-alive entry per session until app quit.
recommendation: Track the owning WebContents id and kill its processes on 'destroyed'/'did-start-navigation'; also cap concurrent sessions per sender.

title: Terminal decodes stdout/stderr chunks with data.toString(), corrupting split multi-byte output
summary: stdout/stderr Buffers are decoded per chunk with Buffer#toString() (implicit UTF-8). Pipe chunk boundaries do not respect character boundaries, so any multi-byte character split across two reads is decoded as U+FFFD on both sides.
failure_scenario: Run any command producing >64KB of CJK/emoji output (e.g. a build log with Chinese messages). Whenever a 3-byte character straddles the 64KB pipe read boundary the user sees replacement characters in the terminal view, and the corruption is unrecoverable because both halves are already decoded before send.
recommendation: Hold a `new StringDecoder('utf8')` per stream (per process) and feed chunks through it; flush on 'end'.

title: Terminal write() can raise an unhandled stdin 'error' and crash the main process
summary: write() calls proc.stdin.write(data) with no callback and no 'error' listener on the stdin stream. A write to a child that has already exited (or closed stdin) emits EPIPE/ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED on that stream, and an 'error' event with no listener is rethrown as an uncaught exception in the main process.
failure_scenario: The user runs a command that ignores stdin and exits quickly (e.g. `ls`), then types into the panel in the window between the child's exit and the 'close' event that removes it from this.processes. proc.stdin.write() emits EPIPE, no listener exists, and the whole Electron main process dies.
recommendation: Pass an error callback to write() (or attach proc.stdin.on('error', ...)) and drop the write when the stream is no longer writable.

title: Concurrent setEnabled(true) starts two tool-gateway HTTP servers and leaks the first
summary: ensureGateway() guards on this.handle, but the guard is checked before the awaited startToolGateway() assigns it. Two overlapping calls both pass the guard, both bind a listener, and the second assignment overwrites the first handle, which is then unreachable and never closed.
failure_scenario: The renderer sends AgentToolEvents.setEnabled twice in the same tick (settings toggle plus the reconnect-time sync after a window reload). Two HTTP servers bind loopback ports; only the second is tracked, so the first keeps its port and its still-valid bearer token for the rest of the process lifetime and onDestroy() never closes it.
recommendation: Store the in-flight promise (`this.starting ??= startToolGateway(...)`) and await that, clearing it on failure.

title: 'Remember' on tuff_read_file grants blanket session-wide file reads, not per-path consent
summary: The confirmation gate is keyed by rememberKey, which for tools without classify() is just the tool name. tuff_read_file is risk 'read', so it is rememberable; one approval with 'remember' ticked skips confirmation for every subsequent path for the rest of the session — contradicting the documented model that consent is per resolved path.
failure_scenario: The user approves `tuff_read_file` for ~/notes/todo.md and ticks 'don't ask again'. The agent's next call reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/Library/Application Support/... with no prompt at all, because the remember key is the string 'tuff_read_file'.
recommendation: Include the resolved path (or its parent directory) in rememberKey for path-scoped tools, the way tuff_mcp_call already narrows to server/tool.

title: OCR processQueue re-entrancy guard is set after an await, allowing duplicate job dispatch
summary: processQueue() checks `if (this.processing) return`, then awaits isQueueDisabled() (a DB/config read) before setting this.processing = true. Two callers that arrive during that await both observe processing === false and both enter the dispatch loop.
evidence:
private async processQueue(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.processing) return
    if (!this.db) return
    if (await this.isQueueDisabled()) return

    this.processing = true
failure_scenario: The 5s polling task (registered at line 382) fires while failJob()'s setImmediate(() => this.processQueue()) at line 1516 is still inside the isQueueDisabled() await. Both loops select the same single ready pending job, both write status='processing' and both call runAgentJob for it — two OCR worker threads on the same image, two attempts increments, and two ocr_results rows for one job.
recommendation: Set this.processing = true synchronously immediately after the guard, before any await, and clear it in the existing finally.

title: OCR start-write skip leaves the job 'pending' with attempts uncounted, so it can never fail out
summary: Under DB write pressure the status='processing'/attempts update is skipped entirely, but the job is dispatched anyway. attemptCount is only assigned to the in-memory row, so the persisted attempts counter never advances for that dispatch.
failure_scenario: A job whose image reliably crashes the native OCR worker is dispatched while the write scheduler is backed up. The process dies (or the app is quit) before failJob() persists anything, so on the next launch the row is still status='pending', attempts=0 — MAX_ATTEMPTS is never reached and the same poisoned job is re-dispatched forever, every 5 seconds.
recommendation: Never skip the claim write: it is the only thing that makes dispatch idempotent. Downgrade the priority/drop policy instead of skipping, or hold the claim in memory and refuse to re-dispatch ids in this.activeJobs.

title: clipboard_history_meta is append-only with no upsert, and reads have no ORDER BY
summary: Both meta writers (clipboard and OCR) plain-INSERT (clipboardId, key, value) rows. There is no unique constraint on (clipboard_id, key) and no delete of the previous value, so each key accumulates one row per update; the reader folds rows into a map with no ordering, so which value wins depends on the query plan.
failure_scenario: One clipboard image walks ocr_status queued -> processing -> retrying -> completed, writing 4+ rows for the key 'ocr_status' (plus ocr_updated_at each time). hydrateWithMeta() has no ORDER BY, so last-row-wins depends on SQLite choosing the clipboard_id index; a plan change (or a covering-index scan) can surface the stale 'processing' value and the UI shows a finished OCR as still running forever.
recommendation: Add a unique index on (clipboard_id, key) and use onConflictDoUpdate; at minimum add `.orderBy(clipboardHistoryMeta.id)` to the hydrate query.

title: Intelligence session stream leaks two intervals and a trace subscription per closed renderer
summary: The subscribe handler parks on a promise that only resolves when a 250ms poller observes streamContext.isCancelled(). That flag is set only by an explicit cancel message from the renderer (server-runtime.ts handleCancel); nothing watches for the sender being destroyed, so a closed/reloaded/crashed window leaves the keepalive interval, the cancel-watcher interval and the runtime trace subscription running for the rest of the process.
failure_scenario: A user watching an agent session reloads the window (or it crashes). handleCancel is never called, so closeStream() never runs: a 10s heartbeat timer, a 250ms poll timer and subscribeSessionTrace stay live and keep formatting/emitting events into a dead sender. Every reload adds another set; onDestroy() at line 677 does not touch open streams either, so quitting still has them armed.
recommendation: Register a webContents 'destroyed'/'render-process-gone' hook that calls handleCancel for that sender's streams, and replace the 250ms poll with the AbortSignal the stream context already exposes.

title: IntelligenceModule.onDestroy boots the agent runtime it is supposed to tear down
summary: onDestroy() awaits waitForAgentRuntime(), which starts the runtime when it has not been started yet. On a module whose onInit failed before startAgentRuntime(), teardown therefore performs a full runtime initialization (builtin tools/agents, orchestrator, agent manager) and only then shuts it down.
failure_scenario: initializeProviderCredentialLifecycle() (line 631) or any earlier onInit step throws, so onInit never reaches startAgentRuntime(). The module manager then calls onDestroy during shutdown, which runs registerBuiltinTools/registerBuiltinAgents and awaits aiCliOrchestrator.initialize() + agentManager.init() while the app is quitting — spawning runtime work at teardown and stalling quit for as long as initialization takes.
recommendation: waitForAgentRuntime() should return immediately when agentRuntimePromise is null; only startAgentRuntime() should create it.

title: Pi runtime start() has no readiness timeout, so a stuck worker hangs every agent run forever
summary: readyPromise is settled only by a 'runtime.ready' message or by the process exiting. There is no timer, and execute() awaits start() before arming its own run timeout, so a forked utility process that spawns but never reports ready blocks every call indefinitely.
failure_scenario: The pi runtime worker hangs during module load (a slow/never-resolving dynamic import, a native module stuck on first load) and never posts runtime.ready. The process is alive, so no 'exit' fires and readyReject is never called. Every subsequent execute() awaits the same pending readyPromise; the conversation UI shows a request that never completes and never times out, and the run timeout that would have rescued it is never installed.
recommendation: Race readyPromise against a bounded timer that kills the child and rejects, mirroring the run-level timeout already used in execute().

title: A throwing post() inside the Pi run executor leaks the run timer and wedges that run id
summary: execute() registers the activeRuns entry (with its timeout handle) and only then calls this.post(...) inside the promise executor. post() throws when the child is gone, and postMessage throws on a non-cloneable payload; the synchronous throw rejects the promise but leaves the map entry and the timer behind.
evidence:
this.activeRuns.set(payload.run.id, {
        ...
        resolve,
        reject,
        timeout
      })
      this.post({ type: 'run.start', payload })
failure_scenario: The utility process exits between `if (!this.child)` at line 370 and the post (or the request payload contains a non-structured-cloneable value). execute() rejects, but activeRuns still holds the run id, so every retry of that run fails with 'Run <id> is already active', and the timeoutMs timer fires later into settleRun on an entry whose promise is already rejected.
recommendation: Wrap the post in try/catch (or post before registering) and delete the activeRuns entry plus clearTimeout on failure.

title: Selection capture clears the clipboard before restoring it, so a partial restore destroys it
summary: restoreClipboard() calls clipboard.clear() and then re-writes each snapshotted format. Any throw mid-loop (or a crash/quit in that window) leaves the user's clipboard emptied or half-restored; the function only reports false afterwards.
failure_scenario: The user has a large image plus RTF on the clipboard and triggers selection capture. snapshotClipboard() skips a format it could not read (line 88 logs and continues) or writeBuffer throws on one of the formats; clear() has already run, so the original clipboard content is gone and only the formats written before the throw survive. The caller returns issueCode 'failed' but cannot undo it.
recommendation: Write the snapshot back with clipboard.write()/writeBuffer per format without a preceding clear(), or verify all buffers are writable before clearing.

title: Selection capture's synthetic Copy is recorded into persisted clipboard history
summary: captureSelection() sends a real Cmd/Ctrl+C to the foreground app to harvest the selection. The clipboard module's native watcher fires on every OS clipboard change and there is no suppression handshake between the two modules, so the selected text is captured and written to clipboard_history as if the user had copied it — and the subsequent restore writes the previous content again as a second new row.
failure_scenario: A user selects a password or a private message in another app and triggers selection capture (or any feature that calls it). The text they never copied is persisted to clipboard_history, shown in the clipboard history UI and forwarded to plugins via forwardClipboardChangeToPlugin; restoring the original clipboard then inserts a duplicate row of the pre-existing entry. Nothing in either module references the other (grep for 'suppress'/'selectionCapture' finds no coordination).
recommendation: Have selection capture mark the window around the synthetic copy (e.g. a shared 'internal clipboard write' token the capture pipeline checks) so those two change events are not persisted.

title: macOS active-app osascript has no timeout and the in-flight guard makes a hang permanent
summary: Every other platform path passes { timeout: ACTIVE_APP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS }, but the macOS osascript call does not. resolveActiveWindowMacOS() dedupes concurrent callers onto macosResolveInFlight, so if that one call never settles the field is never cleared and every later lookup returns the same pending promise.
failure_scenario: AppleScript's 'first application process whose frontmost is true' blocks when the frontmost app is beachballing or a TCC prompt is open. osascript never returns, so the awaited promise stays pending, `this.macosResolveInFlight = null` in the finally never runs, and active-app resolution (and anything downstream that awaits it, e.g. clipboard source attribution) is dead for the rest of the session.
recommendation: Pass { timeout: ACTIVE_APP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer } to the osascript call like every other platform path, and clear macosResolveInFlight on timeout.

title: Selection capture's macOS AppleScript probe also runs without a timeout
summary: captureMacSelectionTextDirectly() runs osascript with no timeout, while the very next step of the same function wraps the copy shortcut in withTimeout(). A hung AppleScript therefore hangs the whole capture even though the module clearly intends every step to be bounded.
failure_scenario: The frontmost app stops answering Apple events (beachball, or a TCC consent sheet is up). The direct-selection probe blocks, so captureSelection() never resolves and the transport handler that awaited it never replies — the caller sees a request that hangs instead of the 'failed'/'unsupported' result the function is designed to return.
recommendation: Wrap the probe in the module's own withTimeout(), or pass { timeout } to execFileAsync.

title: Automation cron rejects day-of-week 7 and ANDs day-of-month with day-of-week
summary: The cron implementation deviates from POSIX cron in two ways: the day-of-week field is validated against 0-6, so the standard '7' spelling of Sunday is rejected as invalid; and cronMatches ANDs all five fields, while cron ORs day-of-month with day-of-week when both are restricted.
evidence:
isValidCronField(fields[4]!, 0, 6)
...
return (
    matchesCronField(date.getMinutes(), fields[0]!, 0, 59) &&
    matchesCronField(date.getHours(), fields[1]!, 0, 23) &&
    matchesCronField(date.getDate(), fields[2]!, 1, 31) &&
    matchesCronField(date.getMonth() + 1, fields[3]!, 1, 12) &&
    matchesCronField(date.getDay(), fields[4]!, 0, 6)
  )
failure_scenario: A user saves an automation with '0 9 * * 7' (Sunday 09:00, a standard spelling) and save() throws 'Automation cron expression must contain five valid fields'. A user who saves '0 9 1 * 1' expecting 'the 1st of the month and every Monday' gets an automation that only ever runs when the 1st falls on a Monday — roughly once a year instead of ~5 times a month.
recommendation: Accept 0-7 for day-of-week (mapping 7 to 0) and OR the day-of-month/day-of-week fields when neither is '*'.

title: expandCommand feeds user text into String.replace as a replacement pattern
summary: $ARGUMENTS is substituted with `content.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS\b/g, args)` where args comes from the user's objective text. A string replacement argument is interpreted as a pattern, so $&, $`, $' and $1 inside the arguments expand instead of being inserted literally.
evidence:
return content
    .replace(/\$ARGUMENTS\b/g, args)
    .replace(/\$(\d)\b/g, (_, index: string) => values[Number(index) - 1] ?? '')
failure_scenario: The user types `/mycommand fix the $& handler` (or pastes text containing $' — common in shell snippets and regex docs). $& expands to the matched text '$ARGUMENTS' and $' expands to the entire remainder of the command body, so the prompt sent to the model contains duplicated or mangled instructions rather than what the user typed.
recommendation: Use a replacer function — `.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS\b/g, () => args)` — which never interprets $ patterns.

title: The documented 10MB per-plugin storage quota is only enforced per file
summary: savePluginFile() compares only the size of the single payload being written against PLUGIN_CONFIG_MAX_SIZE, while getStorageStats() reports that same 10MB as maxSize against the sum of every file. Nothing checks the total, so the advertised per-plugin quota does not exist.
